title: How Colors and Gases Could Help Us Find Tiny Aliens
summary:
If there is life on other worlds, it is probably very tiny. Scientists think it may be microbes, which are living things with just one cell.

Venus is very hot on the ground. But high in its clouds, it is more like Earth. Scientists have seen signs of some gases there. Some think microbes could live in those clouds.

Scientist Noelle Bryan found microbes living very high above Earth. Some of them make bright colors that protect them from strong sunlight. Another scientist, Lígia Coelho, studied those colors. Future telescopes might look for the same colors on faraway planets.

Scientists are also thinking about Mars. Andrew Schuerger and Rachel Harris found a microbe on Earth that can make methane gas even when the air is thin like on Mars. Rovers have found methane on Mars. Schuerger says a rover might only need to dig about 8 inches to find Martian microbes, if they exist.
why_it_matters: These clues could one day help answer a big question kids often ask: are we alone in the universe?
